title: Durham Board Reviewed Special Education Plan and New Transition Guide
executiveSummary: Committee members reviewed updates to the Special Education Plan and school year impacts.
Staff presented an updated Transition Guide and draft Augmentative and Alternative Communication guidelines.
The meeting included reports on student exceptionality data and autism coalition survey results.
studentParentImpact: The meeting focused on updates to special education support, including a revised Transition Guide and draft Augmentative and Alternative Communication guidelines for students across Durham Region. These updates were designed to assist families whose children require special education programs or support during school transitions. The committee also received board-wide exceptionality data and updates on special education impacts for the 2026-2027 school year. Because the agenda was informational, no specific public action or vote was required from parents during this meeting.
policyChanges: Staff shared draft Augmentative and Alternative Communication guidelines and an updated Special Education Plan. No formal policy or procedure was scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: Durham Regional Police presented an update on local police governance to trustees
executiveSummary: Durham Regional Police Service Board leadership delivered a presentation on regional police governance to school board trustees.
Board leadership announced structural title changes, naming Jim Markovski as Chief Education Officer under new provincial regulations.
Student trustees presented their introductory report for the 2026-2027 school year.
studentParentImpact: The presentation on regional police governance highlights ongoing collaboration and oversight between Durham Regional Police Service and local communities, which affects overall school safety and community trust. Meanwhile, new student trustees stepped into their roles to represent student voices across Durham Region for the 2026-2027 school year. Administrative changes split executive responsibilities into distinct business and educational leadership roles following provincial regulations, aiming to improve accountability for student achievement. Families were not required to take action on these informational agenda items.
policyChanges: No policies or board procedures were scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: Trustees Were Set to Accept Resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula
executiveSummary: Trustees were scheduled to accept the resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula.
studentParentImpact: Trustees were set to formally accept the resignation of Trustee Mark Jacula during a special board meeting. A trustee resignation leaves a vacancy on the school board that represents families in the region. The meeting agenda did not include any details on how the board plans to fill the empty seat or any steps for public feedback. Parents and students were not provided with any direct actions or next steps in the agenda document.
policyChanges: No school board policies or procedural rules were scheduled for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.
